newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end lower with Dow, drifting.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end lower with Dow, drifting.

text.p: French shares drifted to close with moderate losses on Monday, lacking domestic momentum and taking their steer from softness on Wall Street, traders said.

The CAC index had been supported by dollar strength since the opening, but faded as investment interest waned in the afternoon, leaving it vulnerable to New York's sway. But the CAC managed to stay above the psychological 2,600 level.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 7.29 points or 0.28 percent at 2,600.26. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 18 at 2,606 from Friday's close.

* Renault dented by profit-taking after 20 percent rise since last Thursday, closes down 4.7 percent at 140 francs. But analysts think the stock should soon recover to 170 franc privatisation price, on the back of restructuring news.
* Lagardere adds 1.79 percent to 171, on speculation the company will win Thomson-CSF in the government's second privatisation attempt. Thomson-CSF ends up 1.66 percent at 183.5.
* Lyonnaise des Eaux climbs 2.23 percent to 595, helped by news of a Budapest water contract.

* The luxury goods group runs into selling, particularly from non-domestic investors, who are concerned about 1996 earnings of DFS, despite LVMH's attempts to explain the situation at the duty free retailer which it is acquiriing.
* AGF rises 2.79 percent, bouncing off the 200 level, after jitters last week over a possible acquisition of troubled insurer GAN, which closes down 0.67 percent at 148.10.
